matching_prompt: Compare the apparent surface gloss of the two objects. Which object looks glossier? Judge gloss, not overall brightness. Answer exactly A if Image A looks glossier, B if Image B looks glossier, or SAME if their surface gloss looks indistinguishable.
matching_system: You are a visual observer performing a surface-gloss matching task. Follow the response format exactly.

prompts.system: Make a visual judgment using the supplied image. Follow the response format exactly.
prompts.T1:
Rate the apparent glossiness of the main object in this image.
Glossiness means how matte or shiny the surface looks.
Use an integer from 0 to 100: 0 = not at all glossy; 100 = extremely glossy.
Judge the visible appearance, not the material name or its physical reflectance.
Return only {"glossiness": <integer>, "status": "ok"}.
If the image is unavailable or the main object cannot be identified, return only
{"glossiness": null, "status": "unrateable"}.
prompts.T2:
Compare the apparent glossiness of the main objects in Image A and Image B.
Which object's surface looks glossier? Judge visible matte versus shiny appearance,
not the object category or the material's physical properties.
Choose A, B, or tie if they appear equally glossy.
Return only a JSON object with keys "choice" and "status".
The value of "choice" must be "A", "B", or "tie"; "status" must be "ok".
If an image is unavailable or its main object cannot be identified, return only
{"choice": null, "status": "unrateable"}.

selection: All original stimuli/pairs/starts; flag prior pilot and original matching development images; no performance-dependent stopping
matching: Same 1..52 bisection, maximum7 decisions, final presented index conversion; A=test B=reference
catch_scope: Main three task responses only; original InternVL practice/catch are not rerun
presentation: One or two images per fresh context; native Qwen preprocessing; bf16 SDPA
